what_office_does.text: The Controller is California’s chief fiscal officer and keeps accounts of all public funds. The office runs the state payroll system, administers unclaimed property laws, and audits and reviews state operations.
what_office_does.label: fact

candidates.name: Malia M. Cohen

says.text: Cohen says taxpayer dollars should be managed with transparency, accountability, and fairness.
says.label: value
says.quote: She is running for re-election to ensure taxpayer dollars are managed with transparency, accountability, and fairness.

says.text: Cohen says budgets should reflect shared values and invest in people, while protecting California’s financial future.
says.label: value

candidates.headline: Cohen says she would manage taxpayer dollars with transparency, accountability, and fairness.
candidates.core_case: Cohen presents transparent and fair financial management as a way to protect California’s financial future. She points to her stated work expanding public financial data and advancing payroll modernization as the foundation for another term.

candidates.name: Herb W Morgan

says.text: Morgan says he would put all state expenditures in an easy-to-use online database with transaction-level details and near real-time reporting.
says.label: prediction
says.quote: placing all expenditures in an easy-to-use online database with transaction-level detail and near real-time reporting

says.text: Morgan emphasizes audits before and after spending to promote efficiency and verify performance and proper use of public funds.
says.label: value

candidates.headline: Morgan says he would publish all state expenditures online with transaction-level detail and near real-time reporting.
candidates.core_case: Morgan proposes detailed, timely public spending information alongside rigorous audits. He says this transparency would build trust and direct resources more effectively to classrooms, communities, and essential programs.
priorities: Transaction-level detail and near real-time reporting

where_they_differ.text: Both emphasize transparency. Cohen stresses fairness and budgets that invest in people, while Morgan focuses on a detailed spending database and audits to improve efficiency and verify how funds are used.
